You are ReproScout, a scientific reproduction agent.
Execute the supplied author's code to answer the task questions. Read /code/README.md
and /REPRODUCING.md first. The controller has already provisioned the author's image:
run commands directly inside this container, not through nested Docker. Work in /code;
data are in /data and /results starts empty. Network access is disabled. Do not alter
experimental code, hardcode answers, or use remembered/published results.
If blocked, submit null values for unanswered questions, with evidence of the blocker
and an optional explanation field. Do not invent values to complete the report. If a required
code change is necessary, explain the blocker instead of silently patching it.
Keep every response in English. Tool outputs include controller-owned artifact IDs and
1-based line numbers. Submit each question's value with evidence from THIS execution.
For plots, use view_image on generated raster files or PDF pages; cite the returned
image artifact without line numbers. Use the submit_report tool with a JSON object keyed by question IDs, for example:
{"q1":{"value":12.3,"evidence":[{"artifact":"artifacts/step-002.stdout.txt",
"line_start":2,"line_end":2}]}}. The example number is not an answer.
An existing file reference does not prove correctness; cite actual computed output.

Frozen development lessons:
# Frozen development lessons, version 1

These rules were curated with Codex assistance from official training runs.
They contain no task answers and are not updated during held-out evaluation.

## L1: Stop searching after confirming an unavailable external dataset

When execution fails on a network request, inspect the loader and check the
provided data directory once. If the required dataset is neither bundled nor
cached, record the failing request and submit unanswered values with blocker
evidence. Do not repeatedly search the entire filesystem or try alternative
internet endpoints in an offline environment.

Source: development capsule-4098236, run
20261117T200334263866Z-capsule-4098236-run-A1, artifacts/step-003.stdout.txt
(network failure), step-004.stdout.txt (loader), and step-007.stdout.txt
(repeated broad search). The run eventually exceeded its context bound.

## L2: Execute a notebook once and inspect its structured outputs

For notebook reproduction, save an executed notebook in the results directory,
then render that executed notebook to the requested presentation format. Locate
relevant output cells using the requested metric labels. Print only the needed
output segments. Avoid dumping full notebook source or raw HTML into context,
and avoid executing the whole experiment again merely to read its output.

Source: development capsule-0940461, run
20261117T200757054830Z-capsule-0940461-run-A1, tool steps 003 through 010.
Source dumping and repeated executions preceded a context-limit failure.

## L3: Discover documentation filenames before chaining commands

List the task directory before assuming that README.md exists. Read whichever
instruction file is actually provided and read REPRODUCING.md separately. A
missing optional README should not prevent required instructions from being read.

Source: development capsule-9168639, run
20261117T200518810509Z-capsule-9168639-run-A1, step-001 and step-002.
The first chained command stopped at a missing README; the next inspected the
available files and recovered.

## Scope

These are development-derived workflow heuristics, not verified universal rules.
They may reduce wasted calls without improving final accuracy. Report both cost
and accuracy, and preserve any adverse effects.

Run 'code.R' using Rscript
Questions:
{
  "q1": "Report the Variances estimate for Exam1.",
  "q2": "Report the Variances estimate for Exam2.",
  "q3": "Report the Variances estimate for Exam3."
}

arguments.command: cd /code && ls -la && echo '--- README ---' && sed -n '1,200p' README.md && echo '--- REPRODUCING ---' && sed -n '1,200p' /REPRODUCING.md && echo '--- code.R head ---' && sed -n '1,220p' code.R

10: # An Example of Compute Capsule
11: 
12: _This is an example compute capsule of the book chapter "Developing and Disseminating Data Analysis Tools for Open Science" in L. Plonsky (Ed.), Open Science in Applied Linguistics._
13: 
14: ## Article
15: Mizumoto, A. (2021, December 14). Developing and disseminating data analysis tools for open science. https://doi.org/10.31219/osf.io/qzawb
16: 
17: ## Code, Data, Results
18: On the left hand column, you can see folders `/code`, `/data`, and `/results`, where code and data are saved. You can upload your own files to the `/code` or `/data` folders using the buttons at the top of the left-side **Files pane**.
19: 
20: Any plots, figures, and results data should be saved in the `/results` directory. At the end of each run, these files will appear in the right-side **Reproducibility pane**, where you can view and download them. When you publish a capsule, the most recent set of results will be preserved as part of the capsule.
21: 
22: ## Environment and Dependencies
23: 
24: Click **Environment** on the left to find a computational environment to accommodate your software (languages, frameworks) or hardware (GPU) requirements. You can then further customize the environment by installing additional packages. The changes you make will be applied the next time your capsule runs. See Code Ocean's help articles on [the computational environment](https://help.codeocean.com/getting-started/the-computational-environment/configuring-your-computational-environment-an-overview) for more information.
25: 
26: ## Environment Caching
27: 
28: The next time you run your capsule after making changes to any part of the environment, a custom environment will be built and cached for future runs.
29: 
30: When you publish a capsule, its computational environment will be preserved with it, thereby ensuring computational reproducibility.
31: 
32: ## Author
33: 
34: [Atsushi MIZUMOTO, Ph.D.](http://mizumot.com "HP")  
35: email: mizumoto[at]kansai-u.ac.jp  
36: Professor of Applied Linguistics

40: --- REPRODUCING ---
41: This [Code Ocean](https://codeocean.com) Compute Capsule will allow you to reproduce the results published by the author on your local machine<sup>1</sup>. Follow the instructions below, or consult [our knowledge base](https://help.codeocean.com/user-manual/sharing-and-finding-published-capsules/exporting-capsules-and-reproducing-results-on-your-local-machine) for more information. Don't hesitate to reach out to [Support](mailto:support@codeocean.com) if you have any questions.
42:

45: # Prerequisites
46: 
47: - [Docker Community Edition (CE)](https://www.docker.com/community-edition)
48: - MATLAB/MOSEK/Stata licenses where applicable
49: 
50: # Instructions
51: 
52: ## The computational environment (Docker image)
53: 
54: This capsule has been published and its environment has been archived and made available on Code Ocean's Docker registry:
55: `registry.codeocean.com/published/72fae0b0-b870-48e9-8173-1e803d5d8c54:v1`
56: 
57: ## Running the capsule to reproduce the results
58: 
59: In your terminal, navigate to the folder where you've extracted the capsule and execute the following command, adjusting parameters as needed:
60: ```shell
61: docker run --platform linux/amd64 --rm \
62:   --workdir /code \
63:   --volume "$PWD/data":/data \
64:   --volume "$PWD/code":/code \
65:   --volume "$PWD/results":/results \
66:   registry.codeocean.com/published/72fae0b0-b870-48e9-8173-1e803d5d8c54:v1 bash run
67: ```
68: --- code.R head ---
69: # read the csv
70: dat <- read.csv("../data/semlavaan.csv", header=TRUE, fileEncoding="CP932")
71: 
72: library(lavaan)
73: # https://lavaan.ugent.be/
74: model <- '
75: Achievement =~ Midterm + Final + Quiz
76: Proficiency =~ Exam1 + Exam2 + Exam3
77: Proficiency ~ Achievement
78: '
79: 
80: fit <- sem(model, data=dat)
81: summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
82: 
83: # Path diagram
84: library(semPlot)
85: 
86: # Standardized estimates
87: png("../results/plot1.png", width = 600, height = 600)
88: semPaths(fit, "std", style="lisrel", # LISREL style
89:          mar=c(6,1,3,1), # margin (bottom, left, up, right)
90:          edge.label.cex=.8, # font size for coefficients
91:          fade=F, # keep the arrow size the same
92:          theme="gray") # gray color
93: dev.off()
